group_assessment.weighting: Observation and interpretation are weighted differently and the split is explicit. As an INDEX of what the field held about WWOX in 2014, and of which primary sources carry which claim, this chapter is authoritative and its reference list is its most valuable content. As EVIDENCE it carries nothing of its own: every datum is a restatement, the two figures are schematics (one explicitly labelled 'Hypothetical'), two load-bearing steps rest on 'unpublished data', and the chapter contradicts itself on the knockout growth phenotype. Additionally, the summariser and the summarised are the same person — the introduction to this issue that restates this chapter is single-authored by this chapter's first author — so the restatement chain carries no independent editorial judgement, which is exactly what the promise test measured.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE PROMISE TEST, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS PAPER WAS READ. In wave 5 this actor read the editor's introduction to this special issue (PMID 25238781) and captured, as a locator, the one-sentence restatement it made of chapter 8: 'Authors conclude that these observations indicate that WWOX is functionally required for cell homeostasis and that its deletion has important consequences contributing to the neoplastic process.' Chapter 8 is this paper. Its own closing proposal, in its abstract, is near-verbatim the same sentence with ONE word changed: the chapter says 'we PROPOSE', the introduction says 'Authors CONCLUDE'. The chapter's own Concluding remarks are hedged in exactly the same direction, and this body sentence is the evidentiary anchor for that: the chapter's terminal generalisation is explicitly SPECULATION. PROPOSE -> CONCLUDE is the seam epistemic_discipline.md and scientist_reading_modes.md 6.2 name — an author's hypothesis reported as an observation — and here the upgrade was performed by the SAME PERSON, single-authoring the introduction that summarised his own chapter.
entries.snippet: Thus, it can be speculated that they function as part of a highly conserved stress response network that is uniquely susceptible to genomic instability in cancer cells.
entries.anchor: Body, Concluding remarks, final paragraph
entries.abstract_snippet: we propose that the gene product of FRA16D, WWOX, is a functionally essential protein that is required for cell homeostasis and that its deletion has important consequences that contribute to the neoplastic process

entries.proposition: THE CHAPTER'S OWN TERMINAL CLAIM IS HEDGED THREE TIMES IN TWO SENTENCES — 'can be argued', 'might have'. Recorded beside the speculation locator because together they establish that the chapter does not CONCLUDE what the introduction says it concludes. It proposes.
entries.snippet: It can be argued that this phenomenon is more complicated and that gene products encompassing these sites might have important roles in stress response and in the neoplastic process.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THIS QUALIFIES THIS ACTOR'S OWN WAVE-5 READING AND THE CORRECTION GOES AGAINST THE MORE INTERESTING STORY. In wave 5, from the editor's introduction plus the 2015 editorial PMID 27551470, this actor recorded that the passive-versus-active framing moved from CONCLUDED (chapter 6, as the editor summarised it in 2014) to DEBATABLE (the 2015 editorial), inside one author's output across thirteen months. Reading chapter 8 shows BOTH framings already coexisted in 2014 in Aqeilan's OWN chapter of that same issue: the Introduction says the evidence 'argues against' passenger status, and the Concluding remarks of the same chapter open by calling it 'debated'. The wave-5 observation stands as stated — it was about the editor's summary of chapter 6 — but the 'movement over thirteen months' reading is WEAKENED, because the hedge was already present in the same issue by the same author. Wave 5 explicitly flagged that the overclaim was available; this is that flag being cashed by reading the primary source.

The Mouse models section states that WWOX ablation causes GROWTH RETARDATION. The bioenergetics section, four sections later, states that the same mice DEVELOP NORMALLY. Reference [7] (PMID 17360458) is cited for both. These cannot both be true of the same animals. This is recorded as a property of THIS document; which restatement is faithful was NOT adjudicated — see the paired locator and the corpus cross-query note.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIGURE 1 PANEL, INSPECTED AS AN IMAGE AT NATIVE RESOLUTION: THE PANEL CARRIES A MECHANISTIC NODE THAT EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE PROSE OR THE CAPTION. The panel draws WWOX acting on PHD2, and draws that single arrow with a literal question mark beside it; PHD2 then inhibits HIF1α, which is hydroxylated (OH), ubiquitinated (Ub) and sent to the proteasome. Measured over the declared text surface: the strings 'PHD2', 'PHD' and 'prolyl' occur ZERO times in the article body and ZERO times in the figure caption. So the figure asserts a route — WWOX to PHD2 to HIF1α degradation — that the article never states in words, and simultaneously marks that route as uncertain with its own question mark. This is only visible by opening the image. It is the honest half of the paper: the caption's language is 'demonstrated', and the panel is where the authors record what is not.

Nodes read off the panel: RAS, Glucose stress, PTEN, AKT(p), AMPK, TSC2(p), mTOR, WWOX (twice), PHD2, HIF1α, HIF1β, Ub, OH, Proteasome, 'HIF1α target genes', 'Glucose uptake', 'Aerobic glycolysis'. The WWOX->PHD2 arrow carries a printed '?'.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIGURE 1 CAPTION NAMES AN ENTITY THE PANEL DOES NOT DRAW. The caption states that inactivation of PTEN and VHL leads to HIF1α accumulation. PTEN is drawn in the panel. VHL is NOT: it appears nowhere in the image. Established by inspecting the image, not by reading the caption. Same class as D-14 in the dismissal ledger, though milder — an omission rather than a contradiction — and it is why 'figures: read' has to mean the pixels were opened.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIGURE 2 PANEL, INSPECTED AS AN IMAGE: THE SAME OMISSION CLASS, AND A UBIQUITIN-LINKAGE CLAIM THE PANEL DOES NOT CARRY. The caption lists ATM substrates as 'H2A.X, CHK2, p53, and ITCH'. The panel draws CHK2(p), H2AX(p) and ITCH(p) — p53 is ABSENT from the image. Separately, the caption asserts K63-LINKED ubiquitination of WWOX; the panel draws only a generic green 'Ub' with no linkage type anywhere in the image. This matters specifically for this repository: epistemic_discipline.md's DEFAULTS THAT BIT US table records polyUb->proteasome as a textbook default that is false as a universal rule, with K63 having context-dependent trafficking roles. Here K63 is invoked for NUCLEAR TRANSLOCATION rather than degradation, which is consistent with that corrected premise — but the linkage type is caption authority only and is not evidenced by the figure.

Nodes read off the panel: ATM dimer, DSB, ATM(p), CHK2(p), H2AX(p), ITCH(p), WWOX, Ub-WWOX, the ITCH/WWOX/ATM ternary complex, 'Efficient DDR'. No p53 node. The ubiquitin is drawn as an unlabelled 'Ub' with no linkage annotation.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE GSK3β ROW OF TABLE 1 CITES THE PAPER AT THE CENTRE OF THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN DISMISSAL-LEDGER CASE D-14. Reference [109] resolves to PMID 22193544 (Wang HY et al., 'WW domain-containing oxidoreductase promotes neuronal differentiation via negative regulation of glycogen synthase kinase 3beta'). D-14 records that in that paper both the main text and the published supplementary legend describe Supplementary Figure A as the co-IP proving 'WWOX does not associate with Tau', while the image contains no Tau blot at all — its two panels are labelled WWOX and GSK3β. This chapter cites that paper only for its GSK3β/neurite-outgrowth result, which is the panel that DOES exist. entries.proposition: 🔴 THE MEASURED ABSENCE, AND THIS IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT OF IT — ON THE HARDEST POSSIBLE TEST CASE. Screened over the 31,756-character article body (front matter, reference list and PMC page chrome excluded): epilep 0, seizure 0, brain 0, CNS 0, WOREE 0, encephalopath 0, intellectual 0, recessive 0, syndrome 0, germline 0. TEN OF TWELVE ARE LITERALLY ZERO. The two non-zeros do not survive inspection: 'ataxia' occurs ONCE and is the expansion of the ATM gene name, quoted here as the anchor; 'neuro' occurs TWICE and BOTH occurrences are inside Table 1 rows (neurodegenerative in the TAU row, neuronal in the GSK3β row), with zero occurrences anywhere in the running prose. This is the field's OWN DEDICATED WWOX CHAPTER, 11 pages, 109 references, published December 2014, and it contains no discussion of a germline WWOX phenotype. Wave 5 predicted this from the rare/common taxonomy measured on PMID 25238781 and PMID 24510053; chapter 8 is the strongest available test of that prediction and it holds. Denominator stated: 12 terms, 1 body of 31,756 characters, 10 exact zeros and 2 hits that are not phenotype content.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE SAME TWO 2010 COPY-NUMBER PAPERS CARRY THE DELETION PREMISE FOR THE THIRD TIME IN THIS ACTOR'S LOT, AND THIS REPOSITORY STILL HOLDS NEITHER. References [27] and [28] here resolve to PMID 20164920 (Beroukhim) and PMID 20164919 (Bignell) — the identical pair that carries the deletion premise in PMID 27551470 (refs 3 and 4) and in PMID 25238781 (refs 6 and 7). Three documents read in this lot, one premise, one pair of primary sources, ABSENT from this ledger at any depth. Note also the wording actually used here: 'most statistically significant common sites' is a statement about statistical ranking, not about frequency, and it is the kind of claim that needs its external anchor before restatement.

entries.proposition: 🔴 A 2014 OPEN QUESTION IN THIS CHAPTER IS ANSWERED BY A 2024 PAPER IN THIS SAME ACTOR'S OWN LOT. The chapter asks whether Wwox deletion cooperates with loss of other tumour suppressors to promote tumorigenesis, after noting that mammary-specific Wwox deletion produced NO tumour phenotype, and it names BRCA1 and BRCA2 among the candidates in the preceding sentences. PMID 38499540 (2024, 'Unveiling the relationship between WWOX and BRCA1 in mammary tumorigenicity and in DNA repair pathway selection') is that experiment, and it was read in full by this actor in wave 3. A decade separates the question from the answer and both sit in one eight-paper lot.

entries.proposition: THE NEGATIVE RESULT THAT SETS UP THAT QUESTION, AND IT IS A REAL NEGATIVE STATED PLAINLY. Mammary-gland-specific WWOX ablation gave no mammary tumour phenotype. The chapter offers three non-exclusive explanations (mosaic MMTV-cre expression, redundancy, a progression-rather-than-initiation role) and settles none.

entries.proposition: THE CHAPTER'S MOST NOVEL MECHANISM RESTS ON A SINGLE REFERENCE, AND THIS REPOSITORY HOLDS THAT REFERENCE ONLY AT PARTIAL DEPTH. The entire DDR section and the whole of Figure 2 are built on reference [34], which resolves to PMID 25331887 (Abu-Odeh et al., PNAS, cited here as 'in press'). Joined against the receipt ledger, 25331887 carries a partial_fulltext_read and no complete read.
